text: The Book of Settlements (Landnámabók) is the most important written source for the settlement of Iceland. The original version of The Book of Settlements is said to be from the 12th century but this version is unfortunately lost. Five manuscripts of The Book of Settlements are preserved. Three of these documents are from the 13th and 14th centuries: Sturlubók, Hauksbók and Melabók. The two others are from the 17th century: Skarðsbók and Þórðarbók. The Book of Settlements is a compilation that tells the story of the first settlers of Iceland, their ancestors and their descendents. The Book of Settlements is thought to have been compiled as a justification for land ownership.
